--- title: Objects and Types --- ## Goals 1. Understand that everything in Python is an object that can be examined. 2. Develop an awareness of types in general and recognize numeric, Boolean, and string types. ## Everything is an object Numbers, strings, and other data you encounter in the Python language are **objects**. This has 3 important consequences for us as programmers: - Objects have *identity*, which we can verify with `id()`. - Objects are said to be of a certain *type*, which we inspect with `type()`. - Objects store *value*; that is, a particular instance of a type is an object that represents data or state. ::: {#18c65eb3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} x = 206 # the value of this number is self-evident ``` ::: ::: {#6454eb70 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} id(x) # we'll have to care about this too much ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 4382131872 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#2898fa4b .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} type(x) # you need to be able to reason about types ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` int ``` ::: ::: ## Fundamental data types ### Numbers See . Python supports two main types of numbers - `int` (intergers, whole numbers), and - `float` (floating point numbers, decimals). ::: {#01514a16 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} x = 1 x print(type(x)) type(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` int ``` ::: ::: Python supports specifying `float` objects via scientific notation. ::: {#54058307 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} 3.14e2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 314.0 ``` ::: ::: Python also supports complex numbers, which will not be used in this class. ::: {#ce6b7fd0 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} z = 1+2j type(z) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` complex ``` ::: ::: Non-finite floating point values are available but somewhat awkward to use. ::: {#4089261a .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} 1/0 # not standard! ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

We will discuss missing values later in working with tabular data. :::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::: ### Truth values The `bool` class is a subclass of `int`. It only has two instances: `True` and `False`. **Mind the capitalization**. ::: {#d5e41a73 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} x = True type(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ``` bool ``` ::: ::: ::: {#895ce39e .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} x = TRUE type(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ### Text data Strings can be defined either with a single quote or a double quotes. ::: {#efc182d5 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} y = "test" type(y) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ``` str ``` ::: ::: ::: {#580d34b2 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} print('allows embedded "double" quotes') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` allows embedded "double" quotes ``` ::: ::: ::: {#cb2454b0 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} print("allows embedded 'single' quotes") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` allows embedded 'single' quotes ``` ::: ::: Strings can also be triple quoted, using single or double quotes, which allows the string to span multiple lines ::: {#832a8d58 .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} s = """line 1 line 2 line 3""" print(s) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` line 1 line 2 line 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3948ba0a .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} "STRING" == "string" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ``` False ``` ::: ::: ::: {#28b6f90a .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} "STRING" < "string" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ## Dynamic typing Python is a dynamically typed language. This means that the Python interpreter does type checking only as code runs, and the type of a variable is allowed to change over its lifetime. Most basic operations will attempt to coerce objects to a consistent type appropriate for the operation. ::: {#cfdee06c .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} 1 + True # add int and bool ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=20} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#85742f28 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} 1 and True # logic on int and bool ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Python treats `0`s and `1`s treated as `False` and `True`. ::: {#4022e27d .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} 0 or 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=22} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#ac67bc38 .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} not 0 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=23} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Why does this example evaluate to something? ::: {#03d2040a .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} 1 > True ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Why does the following throw an error? ::: {#8c664e4c .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} "abc" > 5 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ## Casting Explicit casting between types can be achieved via using the types as functions, eg., `int()`, `float()`, `bool()`, or `str()`. ::: {#2162f1be .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} float("0.5") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=26} ``` 0.5 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#3889e3e6 .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} float(True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=27} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#63824a51 .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} int(1.1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=28} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#784825fe .cell execution_count=29} ``` {.python .cell-code} int("2") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#8c602010 .cell execution_count=30} ``` {.python .cell-code} bool(0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ``` False ``` ::: ::: ::: {#86b10347 .cell execution_count=31} ``` {.python .cell-code} bool("hello") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=31} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#c2d61c39 .cell execution_count=32} ``` {.python .cell-code} str(3.1415926) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=32} ``` '3.1415926' ``` ::: ::: ::: {#6d902d47 .cell execution_count=33} ``` {.python .cell-code} str(True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=33} ``` 'True' ``` ::: :::
